free_tier.stated: Works in Node.js and browsers. Any two instances can easily pair and make a peer-to-peer WebRTC connection to forward TCP/UDP ports (even in browser). No additional signaling server needed. Written in JavaScript.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a tunnel or an address, not an object

retention.stated: not applicable: a live tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: No hosted allowance exists: the software runs on a host that is supplied separately.; ingress: tcp+udp

tooling: The user installs and runs the hsync software (npm i -g hsync, npx hsync, or a browser script); a default hosted hsync.tech server exists and a user can point the software at a self-hosted hsync-server.
chaining: Needs a host from a compute provider.
binding_note: A default hosted hsync.tech server exists but publishes no byte allowance and limits a connection to 4 hours; no free hosted allowance reaches the volume bar. Forwards TCP/UDP ports between two hsync instances, and a user can also run a private hsync-server.
reliability_note: The default hosted hsync.tech server answered HTTP 502 on 2026-11-19.
confidence_note: First-party project README read on 2026-11-19; it names a hosted default server with a 4-hour connection limit, no published byte allowance and a self-host option. The list entry is superseded as the basis.
